correctness.rationale: For any finite plane, every incidence edge has 1 identical, 2q adjacent, 2q^2 cross-incident, and q^3 other partner edges. The four endpoint-route minima are |U-V|, U+V, 1+U+V, and 3-|U+V-1| in law. Integrating these triangular laws gives each density, CDF, mean, second moment, and factored variance. The ratio of two order-parameter densities has derivative proportional to r-q on every unit interval and matches at integer boundaries. The exact-rational independent finite checker passed all 943525 endpoint-coordinate cases and the polynomial identities. Finite cases are not treated as a universal proof.

value.rationale: The complete continuous-distance law is a natural intrinsic-metric and network-transport invariant on an infinite class of finite projective planes. Its strict likelihood-ratio order simultaneously determines the direction of all increasing functionals when a plane order grows; sharp tails and total-variation convergence quantify their global geometry. Its universality over potentially nonisomorphic planes of the same order makes a structural statement beyond a numerical count or the previously known vertex-distance histogram.
